# Security & Audits
Source: https://flash.definitive.fi/docs/security

Security measures, audits, and how Flash's trade engine protects your assets and trade execution

Flash is built on Definitive's institutional-grade trading infrastructure. Every design decision puts the protection of both user funds and trade execution quality first.

> [card] \$3B+
>
> Notional spot volume executed

> [card] 100+
>
> Institutions onboarded

> [card] Millions
>
> Successful Transactions

## Audits

Flash's smart contracts were completed with no major findings:

* [EVM Audit](https://github.com/DefinitiveCo/definitive-public/blob/main/audits/Definitive%20Flash%20EVM%20Audit.pdf)
* [Solana Audit](https://github.com/DefinitiveCo/definitive-public/blob/main/audits/Definitive%20Flash%20SVM%20Audit.pdf)

Additionally, Definitive's smart contracts (the same trade engine that powers Flash) have been audited multiple times by leading security firms, including Zellic, OtterSec, and Cantina. All audits have been completed with no material findings and are available for review [here.](https://docs.definitive.fi/references/audits)

## Settlement contracts

Flash settles trades through audited contracts deployed onchain, and every address is independently verifiable. On EVM, integrators grant the ERC-20 approval to the settlement contract; on Solana, the trading program holds the SPL delegate authority and verifies each order signature.

| Network | Contract | Address |
| - | - | - |
| EVM | Flash settlement contract | [`0x5d00000873b6BF41539e6f5365B0Ff7d3c368f78`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x5d00000873b6BF41539e6f5365B0Ff7d3c368f78) |
| Solana | Flash trading program | [`FLaSHxRVv6G1NCJ2SFGPvQqKUPszuDjaTkBMFCSzEqpJ`](https://explorer.solana.com/address/FLaSHxRVv6G1NCJ2SFGPvQqKUPszuDjaTkBMFCSzEqpJ) |

The EVM contract is deployed at the same address on every supported EVM chain.

## Non-custodial by design

Flash never takes custody of user funds. Tokens remain in the user's wallet until the exact moment a trade executes (even for triggered/conditional orders). There is no intermediate holding contract, no fund transfers to a separate account, and no shared pools.

This applies to every order type, including conditional orders (Limit, TWAP, Stop Loss, Take Profit) that may sit open for days or weeks before execution. During that entire period, the user's tokens remain in their wallet and are visible in their balance.

For a detailed walkthrough of how this works on EVM and Solana, see the [Non-Custodial](/docs/non-custodial) page.

## Trade order signing

Every Flash trade requires two independent authorizations from the user's wallet. Neither alone is sufficient to move funds.

**Layer 1: Onchain approval (one-time per token).** The user grants Flash permission to move a specific token. On EVM, this is a standard ERC-20 approval to the Flash settlement contract. On Solana, this is an SPL token delegation granting the Flash program delegate authority over the spent token's associated token account.

**Layer 2: Offchain order signature (per order).** For each trade, the user signs an offchain payload that authorizes the exact amount and includes an expiration deadline. On EVM, this is an EIP-712 typed-data signature (`evm.orderTypedData`). On Solana, this is an Ed25519 signature over `svm.orderMessage`.

The order signature is a key security control that caps the amount Flash can pull to exactly what the order specifies. Flash cannot execute a swap for more than the signed order authorizes, and cannot execute after the deadline has passed.

## MEV protection

Multiple layers of MEV protection are built into the execution pipeline:

**Offchain order intent.** All Flash trade orders are held offchain and are not visible to MEV bots or other market participants before execution. This mitigates front-running and other malicious attacks compared to protocols that publicize trades in public mempools.

**Pre-execution simulation.** Before submitting any transaction onchain, Flash simulates the swap offchain to detect malicious or compromised liquidity pools.

**Private submission.** Orders are submitted through private channels, preventing front-running and sandwich attacks by keeping trade intent out of the public mempool.

**Slippage optimization.** Flash re-evaluates pricing at execution time and applies tight slippage to make sandwich attacks economically unfeasible.

## API key security

Flash requires an API key passed via the `x-definitive-api-key` header on every request. Keys are scoped to each specific integrator, and funds are never commingled amongst integrators.

A leaked API key cannot move funds on its own. Every trade still requires the user's signed order and a valid onchain allowance, and an API key produces neither. If a key is exposed, revoke it and issue a replacement from the Flash integrator dashboard.

## System status

Monitor real-time Flash API uptime and incidents at [status.definitive.fi](https://status.definitive.fi/).

## Responsible disclosure

If you discover a security vulnerability in Flash's smart contracts or infrastructure, please email [security@definitive.fi](mailto:security@definitive.fi).


# Solana Overview
Source: https://flash.definitive.fi/docs/solana-overview

How quoting, routing, delegation, and signing work for Flash orders on Solana.

Flash API supports advanced orders for any SPL token on Solana, including Token-2022 mints. Aggregated liquidity across Solana's DEXs and liquidity sources feeds the Flash smart order router.

This page walks through how quoting, routing, and signing work on Solana at a high level. For the full endpoint reference, see [Quote](/docs/api-reference/flash/quote) and [Order](/docs/api-reference/flash/order).

Base URL for all Flash API requests: `https://flash.definitive.fi/v1`

## Solana order flow

Every Solana order follows four steps: quote, delegate, sign, submit. Before your first trade of a token, you also create the token accounts the swap needs. The user's wallet must authorize every action. Flash never takes custody of funds.

**1. Get a quote**

Call `POST /quote` with the asset pair (`targetAsset` / `contraAsset` and their `targetChain` / `contraChain`), `side` (`buy` or `sell`), `qty` (a decimal string in the spent asset's units: `contraAsset` on a buy, `targetAsset` on a sell), and `orderType`. For a same-chain Solana order, both assets are base58 mint addresses and both chains are `solana`. Crosschain orders use different chain values and require `recipientAddress`; see [Crosschain Orders](/docs/crosschain-orders). Pass `funderAddress` (your base58 wallet address) so Flash can build the signing payloads. Flash's smart order router evaluates routes across Solana liquidity sources and returns the best pricing.

The response includes:

* `quoteId`: reference ID to lock this pricing on submit
* `bridgeQuoteId` *(crosschain, conditional)*: bridge quote to echo back on submit when non-null
* `from` / `to`: the spent and received legs, each with `asset` (`target` or `contra`), `amount`, and `notional`
* `fees.estimatedFeeNotional`: total fee (gas, trading, integrator) in USD notional
* `svm.orderMessage`: the UTF-8 message the user must Ed25519-sign
* `svm.nonce` and `svm.deadline`: order nonce and Unix-seconds expiry, echoed back at submit so the program can rebuild the signed message
* `svm.ataSetupIxs` *(conditional)*: instructions that create your input and/or output token accounts, included when either does not yet exist onchain (see the next step)
* `svm.delegateIx` *(conditional)*: a Solana instruction granting the Flash program delegate authority over the spent token, included when the existing delegation is insufficient
* `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx` *(conditional)*: a sponsor-paid alternative to `delegateIx` (see below)
* `wrap` *(conditional)*: native-SOL wrapping instructions, included when the quote spends native SOL

On Solana quotes the `evm` block is always null.

**2. Create your token accounts (first time per token)**

The swap moves tokens through your funder wallet's associated token accounts (ATAs), so the input and output ATAs must exist before the order runs. When either is missing on-chain, the quote returns `svm.ataSetupIxs`: one idempotent create-associated-token-account instruction per missing account, with your funder wallet in the payer slot. These instructions are not included in the `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx`, as Definitive does not sponsor token account creation.

Send these instructions from your funder wallet before delegating, signing, and submitting. Your funder wallet pays the account rent (about 0.002 SOL per account, more for Token-2022 mints with extensions) and owns the accounts.

The instructions are idempotent, so re-sending them is a safe no-op, and `svm.ataSetupIxs` is null once both accounts already exist. When a single order needs several onchain setup actions, run them in this order: create token accounts, wrap native SOL (if the quote spends native SOL), then delegate. You do not need a separate transaction per step; see [combining setup instructions into one transaction](#combining-setup-instructions-into-one-transaction).

> [!NOTE]
>
> Definitive does not sponsor token account creation. Execute `svm.ataSetupIxs` whenever the quote returns it, they are not created for you.

**3. Handle token delegation (one-time per token)**

Solana has no ERC-20 approval. Instead, Flash grants itself delegate authority over the spent token's associated token account using an SPL `Approve` instruction scoped to the Flash program. This is the Solana equivalent of an EVM token approval and is required once per token per wallet. After the delegation lands onchain, future orders for the same token skip this step. With `forceMinimalAllowance: true`, the delegation is instead sized to the cumulative amount of this quote plus unfilled open orders and is re-issued whenever the existing delegated amount differs from it. See [Minimal authorization](/docs/minimal-authorization).

The quote returns the delegation in one of two mutually exclusive forms, and `svm.delegateIx` is the default:

* `svm.delegateIx`: a raw instruction. Wrap it in a transaction, sign it with your funder wallet, and submit it to Solana yourself, paying the network fee. Build and test against this path, and keep SOL in the funder wallet for it.
* `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx`: a base64 `VersionedTransaction`. Sign it with your funder wallet and echo it back as `svmSponsoredDelegateTx` at submit, and Definitive covers the network fee and broadcasts it. Sponsorship is off for new accounts, so do not assume this will appear.

At most one of the two is non-null, and when both are null the existing delegation already covers this order. With `forceMinimalAllowance: true`, both are null only when the existing delegated amount exactly equals the cumulative amount.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The delegation and the order signature are separate actions by design. The delegation is an onchain (or sponsored) transaction that grants the Flash program authority to pull the spent token. The order signature is a gasless offchain Ed25519 signature. They cannot be batched into a single user interaction.

You do not need a separate transaction for the delegation. See [combining setup instructions into one transaction](#combining-setup-instructions-into-one-transaction).

**4. Sign the order payload**

The user signs `svm.orderMessage` with their wallet's Ed25519 key, producing a 64-byte signature. Encode it as base58 and pass it as `userSignature`. The message is plaintext, so a wallet's message-signing flow surfaces the order's mint and amount to the user.

```ts theme={null}
import { Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import nacl from "tweetnacl";
import bs58 from "bs58";

const keypair = Keypair.fromSecretKey(bs58.decode("..."));
const message = new TextEncoder().encode(quote.svm.orderMessage);
const signature = nacl.sign.detached(message, keypair.secretKey);
const userSignature = bs58.encode(signature);
```

The signed message commits to the order details (input mint, total, nonce, deadline) and to the Flash program and your Definitive trading group, so it cannot be replayed against another order or program. To check the message before signing, see [Verifying the order message](#verifying-the-order-message).

**5. Submit the order**

Call `POST /order` with the original trade parameters plus `funderAddress`, `quoteId`, `userSignature`, `svmNonce`, and `svmDeadline` (echoed back unchanged from the quote). For a crosschain market order, also send `recipientAddress` and echo a non-null `bridgeQuoteId`. If the quote returned `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx`, also sign it and include it as `svmSponsoredDelegateTx`. The EVM-only fields (`evmOrderTypedData`, `evmPermitTypedData`, `evmPermitSignature`) must not be present on Solana submissions.

Flash handles priority fees, MEV protection, simulation, and onchain landing. The response returns an `orderId` for tracking.

## Combining setup instructions into one transaction

`svm.ataSetupIxs` and `svm.delegateIx` are both plain instructions, so you can send them in a single Solana transaction rather than one per step. Keep the documented ordering inside that transaction: token account creation first, then the native SOL wrap instructions if the quote returned them, then delegation. Solana runs instructions in order, and the `Approve` needs the input token account to exist before it runs; on the native SOL path, that account is created and funded by the wrap instructions ahead of it. Broadcast the transaction and wait for confirmation before calling `POST /order`, which rejects the submission when the delegation does not cover the order total, or, on same-chain orders, when the funder's output token account is still missing.

If you run your own sponsor wallet, this is also where you cover the user's costs. Set the sponsor wallet as the transaction fee payer and have it co-sign alongside the funder wallet, which still signs as the token account authority for the `Approve` and as the source of any wrapped SOL. To have the sponsor pay account rent as well, rebuild the create-associated-token-account instructions with the sponsor wallet in the payer slot and the funder wallet as the account owner. The instructions the quote returns put the funder wallet in both slots, in `svm.ataSetupIxs` and in `wrap.svmInstructions`.

Wallet providers that support a separate Solana fee payer document this co-signing pattern in their own gas sponsorship guides.

## Native SOL and wSOL

Flash settles Solana trades against SPL tokens. The mint `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` is the wSOL mint used in Flash requests.

To spend native SOL, set the spent asset to `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` and set `svmUseNativeSOL: true` on the quote request. For `side: "sell"`, the spent asset is `targetAsset`; for `side: "buy"`, it is `contraAsset`. You must also include `funderAddress` so Flash can build the wrapping instructions.

The quote response returns `wrap.svmInstructions`. Send those instructions from the funder wallet before signing and submitting the order. The order itself uses the wSOL mint, plus the `svm.orderMessage`, `svm.nonce`, and `svm.deadline` returned by the quote.

For native-SOL quotes, `wrap.svmInstructions` creates your wSOL (input) account itself, so `svm.ataSetupIxs` only covers the output account. Land the onchain steps in order, `ataSetupIxs`, then the wrap instructions, then delegation, before you sign and submit. (The order signature is offchain; it only needs to be included in the submit.)

If you omit `svmUseNativeSOL`, `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` is treated as an ordinary existing wSOL balance. When `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` is the buy asset, the output is wSOL. Flash does not currently support native SOL as the output asset.

## Signer support

Flash orders on Solana must be signed by a standard Ed25519 keypair. The funder wallet signs `svm.orderMessage` directly, and Flash verifies the 64-byte Ed25519 signature against the funder's public key. A composed order with an attached take-profit / stop-loss pair signs a second message the same way — see [Bracket Orders](/docs/brackets#on-solana).

Multisig wallets that sign through a program-derived address cannot produce a direct Ed25519 order signature. Owners of such a multisig should trade from a dedicated wallet (or a future delegate-registration flow) rather than the multisig address itself.

## Verifying the order message

`svm.orderMessage` is plaintext in this format:

```
DFS|m=<input_mint>|t=<order_total>|h=<order_hash>
```

* `m`: the base58 mint of the spent token
* `t`: the order total in the spent token's base units
* `h`: a truncated, unkeyed SHA-256 hash that you can recompute to confirm what the signature authorizes

```
h = base58( SHA256( "DFS_ORDER_V1" ‖ output_token_account ‖ nonce ‖ deadline ‖ input_token_account ‖ program_id ‖ group )[0:16] )
```

| Field | Value | Encoding |
| - | - | - |
| `"DFS_ORDER_V1"` | Domain tag | 12 ASCII bytes, no length prefix or terminator |
| `output_token_account` | Your funder wallet's associated token account for the received mint. On crosschain quotes, the Flash program's `flash_orders` PDA instead | Raw 32 bytes, decoded from base58 |
| `nonce` | `svm.nonce` from the quote | u64, little-endian (8 bytes) |
| `deadline` | `svm.deadline` from the quote, in Unix seconds | i64, little-endian (8 bytes) |
| `input_token_account` | Your funder wallet's associated token account for the spent mint `m` | Raw 32 bytes, decoded from base58 |
| `program_id` | The Flash program: `FLaSHxRVv6G1NCJ2SFGPvQqKUPszuDjaTkBMFCSzEqpJ` | Raw 32 bytes, decoded from base58 |
| `group` | Your Definitive trading group on Solana. Contact Definitive with your organization ID to get it | Raw 32 bytes, decoded from base58 |

Derive each associated token account with the mint's own token program (SPL Token or Token-2022).

## Slippage and price protection

You configure trader slippage or maximum price impact on the quote request. The signed order message does not contain a minimum-output amount, so Flash resolves the applicable protection when the swap is built and submitted:

| Order type | How price is protected |
| - | - |
| **Market** | For a standard market order, the keeper computes a minimum-output amount from the quoted output and `maxSlippage`. If the swap cannot meet the applicable bound, the transaction reverts and no funds move. |
| **Limit** | The limit price is the binding constraint. The order only fills at or better than the limit price. |
| **Stop, Stop Loss, Take Profit, TWAP** | These execute at a future time. The keeper re-evaluates pricing and applies `maxPriceImpact` against the reference price available at execution. |

Immediately before submission, the solver also applies an internal onchain-slippage bound against a fresh simulation. This dynamic bound accounts for factors such as Solana block times, pair volatility, and MEV activity. See [Slippage and price protection](/docs/placing-orders#slippage-and-price-protection) for the complete model.

## Routing and MEV protection

Flash routes every order through a smart order router that aggregates Solana's DEXs and liquidity sources. Before submitting any transaction onchain, Flash simulates the swap offchain to optimize for best execution and to guard against malicious or compromised liquidity.

Settlement runs through the Definitive Flash Solana program: the program verifies the user's Ed25519 signature, pulls the spent token via the granted delegation, executes the swap, and routes the output and fees, all in a single atomic transaction. Orders are landed with priority fees and MEV-protected inclusion.

> [card] [EVM Overview](/docs/evm-overview)
>
> How quoting, routing, approvals, and signing work on EVM chains.

> [card] [Supported Chains](/docs/supported-chains)
>
> Full chain and asset coverage.

| `base` | `8453` | `https://mainnet.base.org` |
| `bsc` | `56` | `https://bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org` |
| `ethereum` | `1` | `https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com` |
| `hyperevm` | `999` | `https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm` |
| `ink` | `57073` | `https://rpc-gel.inkonchain.com` |
| `monad` | `143` | `https://rpc.monad.xyz` |
| `optimism` | `10` | `https://mainnet.optimism.io` |
| `plasma` | `9745` | `https://rpc.plasma.to` |
| `polygon` | `137` | `https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com` |
| `robinhood` | `4663` | `https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com` |
| `solana` | Not applicable | `https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com` |

Crosschain orders are live between supported chains when a route is available. See [Crosschain Orders](/docs/crosschain-orders) for the required fields and example.


# Trailing Stop Orders
Source: https://flash.definitive.fi/docs/trailing-stop

End-to-end trailing-stop and trailing-stop-limit orders on EVM and Solana with runnable TypeScript.

A trailing stop follows the market instead of resting at a fixed trigger price. It tracks a watermark of the target asset's USD price, the highest price seen for a sell or the lowest for a buy, and fires when the price retraces from that watermark by `trailPercent`. The trigger only ever moves in your favour: a pullback never loosens it.

Trailing orders take a `trailingStop` block instead of `triggers`. The signing and submit plumbing is identical to a [stop-loss](/docs/trigger-orders); only the request fields differ. For the concepts behind the shared parameters, see [Placing Orders](/docs/placing-orders).

| Order type | `side` | Tracks | Fires when | Executes as |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `trailing-stop` | `sell` | High-water mark | Price falls to or below `watermark × (1 − trailPercent)` | Market sell |
| `trailing-stop` | `buy` | Low-water mark | Price rises to or above `watermark × (1 + trailPercent)` | Market buy |
| `trailing-stop-limit` | `sell` or `buy` | As above | As above | Limit order at the effective trigger price |

`qty` follows the usual rule: contra units on a buy, target units on a sell. Trailing orders are same-chain only.

## The `trailingStop` block

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `trailPercent` | yes | Trail distance as a fraction of the watermark: `"0.05"` is 5%. Between `0.005` (0.5%) and `0.5` (50%) inclusive. |
| `activationPrice` | no | USD price of the target asset at which the trail arms. Until the market reaches it (at or above for a sell, at or below for a buy) the order tracks nothing. Omit to arm at the first price Flash sees after placement. |

Neither trailing type takes a limit price: `limitNotionalPrice` and `limitCrossPrice` are rejected, and so is `triggers`. The limit of a `trailing-stop-limit` is the effective trigger price Flash derives from the watermark when the trail fires. `expireTime` is optional, as on other trigger types: set it for good-til-time, omit it for good-til-cancelled.

## How the trail moves

Once armed, every price Flash observes does two things, in order: it ratchets the watermark (up for a sell, down for a buy) and it is compared against the effective trigger computed from that updated watermark. A freshly armed trail can never fire on the price that armed it, because the trigger sits `trailPercent` away from it. This also means a trailing order never closes `REASON_ORDER_TRIGGERED_ON_ENTRY`.

Sell with `trailPercent: "0.05"` and no activation price:

| Price | High-water mark | Effective trigger | What happens |
| - | - | - | - |
| 100 | 100 | 95 | Arms. Tracking starts |
| 110 | 110 | 104.5 | New high raises the trigger |
| 105 | 110 | 104.5 | Trigger stays where it was |
| 120 | 120 | 114 | New high raises the trigger again |
| 114 | 120 | 114 | Fires: a market sell for `qty`, or a limit sell at 114 on `trailing-stop-limit` |

Buy with `trailPercent: "0.05"` and `activationPrice: "100"`:

| Price | Low-water mark | Effective trigger | What happens |
| - | - | - | - |
| 120 | — | — | Waiting for activation |
| 100 | 100 | 105 | Arms. Tracking starts |
| 80 | 80 | 84 | New low lowers the trigger |
| 83 | 80 | 84 | Trigger stays where it was |
| 84 | 80 | 84 | Fires: a market buy for `qty`, or a limit buy at 84 on `trailing-stop-limit` |

The reference price is the same USD price of the target asset that `notionalPrice` triggers evaluate against. There is no pair-rate (`crossPrice`) form of a trailing stop.

## Execution when it fires

**`trailing-stop`** places a market order. Like a `stop-loss` it is designed to prioritize exiting once the trail is breached, so when you omit `maxPriceImpact` it executes under the same deliberately wide 50% default, on both sells and buys. Set `maxPriceImpact` in the quote for a tighter bound when price matters more than exiting; an explicit value is authoritative when the trail fires. If the available route exceeds the bound, the swap does not execute and no funds move. See [Stop-loss execution and price protection](/docs/trigger-orders#stop-loss-execution-and-price-protection) for the trade-off.

**`trailing-stop-limit`** places a limit order at the effective trigger price at the moment of firing: a sell fills at or above it, a buy at or below it. It never fills worse than the trail, but it can rest unfilled if the market keeps moving away. Once it has fired it is an ordinary resting limit order and can be cancelled by its `orderId`.

## End-to-end example: trailing stop

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Prerequisites.** EVM examples use [`viem`](https://viem.sh); Solana examples use `@solana/web3.js`, `tweetnacl`, and `bs58`. All requests go to `https://flash.definitive.fi/v1` with your key in the `x-definitive-api-key` header. The public integrator key `dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b` is safe for development. The onchain steps also need an RPC endpoint and the funder wallet's key, supplied here through environment variables.

> [accordion] EVM
>
> Sell 0.05 WETH for USDC on Base once WETH has reached \$4,000 and then falls 5% from its high. On a sell, `qty` is denominated in the target asset (WETH). If the spent token needs an allowance, the quote returns `evm.approveTx` (or `evm.permitTypedData` on the Permit2 path); handle whichever it returns, then sign the order payload and submit.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { createWalletClient, createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
> import { base } from "viem/chains";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`);
> const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain: base, transport: http(process.env.EVM_RPC_URL) });
> const publicClient = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http(process.env.EVM_RPC_URL) });
>
> const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
>   fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
>     method: "POST",
>     headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>     body: JSON.stringify(body),
>   }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> const order = {
>   targetChain: "base",
>   contraChain: "base",
>   targetAsset: "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
>   contraAsset: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
>   side: "sell",
>   qty: "0.05",
>   orderType: "trailing-stop",
>   trailingStop: { trailPercent: "0.05", activationPrice: "4000" }, // arm at $4,000, trail 5% below the high
>   maxPriceImpact: "0.1", // reject execution above 10% price impact
> };
>
> const quote = await post("/quote", { ...order, funderAddress: account.address });
>
> if (quote.evm.approveTx) {
>   const hash = await wallet.sendTransaction({
>     to: quote.evm.approveTx.to,
>     data: quote.evm.approveTx.data,
>     value: 0n,
>   });
>   await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });
> }
>
> let permitFields = {};
> if (quote.evm.permitTypedData) {
>   const evmPermitSignature = await account.signTypedData(JSON.parse(quote.evm.permitTypedData));
>   permitFields = { evmPermitTypedData: quote.evm.permitTypedData, evmPermitSignature };
> }
>
> const { domain, types, primaryType, message } = JSON.parse(quote.evm.orderTypedData);
> const userSignature = await account.signTypedData({ domain, types, primaryType, message });
>
> const { orderId } = await post("/order", {
>   ...order,
>   funderAddress: account.address,
>   quoteId: quote.quoteId,
>   userSignature,
>   evmOrderTypedData: quote.evm.orderTypedData,
>   ...permitFields,
> });
>
> console.log("orderId", orderId);
> ```

> [accordion] SVM (Solana)
>
> Sell 5 WSOL for USDC if WSOL falls 5% from its high, arming at the current price. On a sell, `qty` is denominated in the target asset (WSOL). Before the first trade of a token the swap needs the funder's token accounts (`svm.ataSetupIxs`) and a delegation (`svm.delegateIx` or a sponsor-paid `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx`). Run the onchain steps in order, then sign the order message offchain and submit.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import {
>   Connection,
>   Keypair,
>   PublicKey,
>   TransactionInstruction,
>   TransactionMessage,
>   VersionedTransaction,
> } from "@solana/web3.js";
> import nacl from "tweetnacl";
> import bs58 from "bs58";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");
> const funder = Keypair.fromSecretKey(bs58.decode(process.env.SOLANA_SECRET_KEY!));
>
> const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
>   fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
>     method: "POST",
>     headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>     body: JSON.stringify(body),
>   }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> const toIx = (ix: any) =>
>   new TransactionInstruction({
>     programId: new PublicKey(ix.programId),
>     keys: ix.accounts.map((a: any) => ({
>       pubkey: new PublicKey(a.pubkey),
>       isSigner: a.isSigner,
>       isWritable: a.isWritable,
>     })),
>     data: Buffer.from(bs58.decode(ix.data)),
>   });
>
> async function sendIxs(instructions: any[]) {
>   const { blockhash } = await connection.getLatestBlockhash();
>   const message = new TransactionMessage({
>     payerKey: funder.publicKey,
>     recentBlockhash: blockhash,
>     instructions: instructions.map(toIx),
>   }).compileToV0Message();
>   const tx = new VersionedTransaction(message);
>   tx.sign([funder]);
>   const sig = await connection.sendRawTransaction(tx.serialize());
>   await connection.confirmTransaction(sig, "confirmed");
> }
>
> const order = {
>   targetChain: "solana",
>   contraChain: "solana",
>   targetAsset: "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112", // WSOL
>   contraAsset: "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v", // USDC
>   side: "sell",
>   qty: "5",
>   orderType: "trailing-stop",
>   trailingStop: { trailPercent: "0.05" }, // arm now, trail 5% below the high
>   maxPriceImpact: "0.1", // reject execution above 10% price impact
> };
>
> const quote = await post("/quote", { ...order, funderAddress: funder.publicKey.toBase58() });
>
> if (quote.svm.ataSetupIxs) await sendIxs(quote.svm.ataSetupIxs);
>
> let delegateFields = {};
> if (quote.svm.sponsoredDelegateTx) {
>   const tx = VersionedTransaction.deserialize(Buffer.from(quote.svm.sponsoredDelegateTx, "base64"));
>   tx.sign([funder]);
>   delegateFields = { svmSponsoredDelegateTx: Buffer.from(tx.serialize()).toString("base64") };
> } else if (quote.svm.delegateIx) {
>   await sendIxs([quote.svm.delegateIx]);
> }
>
> const signature = nacl.sign.detached(new TextEncoder().encode(quote.svm.orderMessage), funder.secretKey);
> const userSignature = bs58.encode(signature);
>
> const { orderId } = await post("/order", {
>   ...order,
>   funderAddress: funder.publicKey.toBase58(),
>   quoteId: quote.quoteId,
>   userSignature,
>   svmNonce: quote.svm.nonce,
>   svmDeadline: quote.svm.deadline,
>   ...delegateFields,
> });
>
> console.log("orderId", orderId);
> ```

## Trailing stop-limit and trailing buys

The flow above works unchanged for the other shapes. Swap the `order` block for one of these; everything else (approval or delegation, signing, submit) stays the same.

**Trailing stop-limit: sell 0.05 WETH when it falls 3% from its high, as a limit order at the trail.**

```jsonc theme={null}
{
  "targetChain": "base",
  "contraChain": "base",
  "targetAsset": "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
  "contraAsset": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
  "side": "sell",
  "qty": "0.05",
  "orderType": "trailing-stop-limit",
  "trailingStop": { "trailPercent": "0.03" }
}
```

**Trailing buy: spend 100 USDC on WETH once WETH has dipped to \$3,000 and then bounces 5% off its low.**

On a buy, `qty` is denominated in the contra asset (USDC).

```jsonc theme={null}
{
  "targetChain": "base",
  "contraChain": "base",
  "targetAsset": "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
  "contraAsset": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
  "side": "buy",
  "qty": "100",
  "orderType": "trailing-stop",
  "trailingStop": { "trailPercent": "0.05", "activationPrice": "3000" }
}
```

## Reading the trail

Order reads return the trail as submitted plus its state under `trailingStop`, with `trigger` null. `GET /orders/{orderId}` for the EVM example above, a little after the trail armed:

```jsonc theme={null}
{
  "orderId": "a1b2c3d4-…",
  "orderType": "trailing-stop",
  "side": "sell",
  "status": "ORDER_STATUS_ACCEPTED",
  "trigger": null,
  "trailingStop": {
    "trailPercent": "0.05",
    "activationPrice": "4000",
    "activated": true,
    "watermarkPrice": "4120.5",
    "effectiveTriggerPrice": "3914.475",
    "watermarkUpdatedAt": "2026-10-29T14:03:12Z"
  }
  // …other order fields
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `trailPercent` | The trail as submitted, a fraction. |
| `activationPrice` | The USD activation price as submitted; `null` when the trail armed immediately. |
| `activated` | `true` once the trail has armed, as last persisted. `false` until the first watermark is saved, even without an `activationPrice`. |
| `watermarkPrice` | The USD high-water mark (sell) or low-water mark (buy) the trail is measured from, as last persisted. `null` until the first watermark is saved. |
| `effectiveTriggerPrice` | The USD price the order fires at: the watermark less `trailPercent` on a sell, plus it on a buy. `null` until the first watermark is saved. |
| `watermarkUpdatedAt` | When `watermarkPrice` last moved; `null` until it has. |

Flash fires on the watermark it holds in memory and persists that watermark on a throttle: at most once every 5 seconds per order, and only once a minute while the trigger has moved less than 1% since the last save. The values you read are therefore the last saved watermark, and the live trigger can sit slightly ahead of them. Firing is never delayed by persistence.

The [Orders WebSocket](/docs/api-reference/flash/websocket-orders) carries the same `trailingStop` block on every frame for the order, so a stream shows the trigger ratcheting as the market moves.

## Lifecycle

* **Expiry.** `expireTime` is optional. Omit it for good-til-cancelled; set an ISO-8601 timestamp for good-til-time. An unarmed or armed-but-unfired trail that reaches its expiry is closed `REASON_ORDER_EXPIRED`.
* **No updates.** `PATCH /orders/{orderId}` returns `422` for both trailing types. To change `trailPercent` or `activationPrice`, cancel and place a new order. The new order arms from the price at that moment, not from the old watermark.
* **Cancelling.** Cancel at any point before the fire with [`POST /orders/{orderId}/cancel`](/docs/cancelling-orders). After the fire, a `trailing-stop-limit` is a resting limit order and can still be cancelled by the same `orderId`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To track the order after submit, poll `GET /orders` or stream live updates over the [Orders WebSocket](/docs/api-reference/flash/websocket-orders).

> [card] [Trigger Orders](/docs/trigger-orders)
>
> Fixed-price stop, stop-loss, and take-profit orders.

> [card] [Placing Orders](/docs/placing-orders)
>
> The full parameter reference for every order type.


# Trigger Orders
Source: https://flash.definitive.fi/docs/trigger-orders

End-to-end stop, stop-loss, and take-profit orders on EVM and Solana with runnable TypeScript.

Trigger orders fire on a price condition rather than a fixed limit. Each entry in `triggers` carries exactly one of `notionalPrice` (the USD price of the target asset) or `crossPrice` (the pair rate, target / contra), plus a `triggerType`: `lower` fires when the market drops to or below the price, `upper` fires when it rises to or above. For the concepts behind the parameters, see [Placing Orders](/docs/placing-orders).

This page covers three single-trigger types: `stop`, `stop-loss`, and `take-profit`. The signing and submit plumbing is identical to a market order; only the request fields differ, and each type has a fixed `side` and, for two of them, a fixed `triggerType`. Each is a single leg. To put both a take-profit and a stop-loss on a token you already hold as one linked order, place a standalone `bracket` instead; to attach the pair to a new `market`, `limit`, or `twap` order, use `attachedBracket`. Both are covered in [Bracket Orders](/docs/brackets). For a stop whose trigger follows the market instead of resting at a fixed price, see [Trailing Stop Orders](/docs/trailing-stop).

| Order type | `side` | `triggerType` | Fires when |
| - | - | - | - |
| `stop-loss` | `sell` | `lower` | Price falls to or below the trigger |
| `take-profit` | `sell` | `upper` | Price rises to or above the trigger |
| `stop` | `buy` | `upper` (typical) | Price rises to or above the trigger (breakout entry) |

Each of these takes exactly one trigger. `qty` follows the usual rule: contra units on a buy, target units on a sell. The examples below use `notionalPrice`; substitute `crossPrice` to fire on the pair rate instead of the dollar price — `{ "crossPrice": "3000", "triggerType": "lower" }` fires when WETH falls to 3,000 USDC per WETH. Exactly one of the two is required on every trigger.

## Stop-loss execution and price protection

A stop-loss without a limit price is designed to prioritize exiting once the trigger is breached. In fast cascades, rug pulls, or fragmented low-liquidity markets, a tight execution bound can repeatedly reject the available route and leave you holding the asset as its price continues to fall. Triggered market orders therefore use a deliberately wide default maximum price impact of 50%.

Set `maxPriceImpact` in the quote when you need a different trade-off. An explicit value remains authoritative when the trigger executes, for both `notionalPrice` and `crossPrice` triggers; Flash does not replace it with the 50% default. If the available route exceeds that bound, the swap does not execute and no funds move.

Use `maxPriceImpact` to choose between two execution priorities:

* **Exit priority** — Keep a wider maximum price impact. The order fires as soon as the reference price crosses the trigger and accepts more price impact when liquidity is thin.
* **Price priority** — Set a tighter maximum price impact. After the trigger fires, Flash executes only when the simulated route satisfies your bound. The order may not fill if liquidity disappears or the market moves too quickly.

These are execution priorities, not separate API mode values. Configure the trade-off with `maxPriceImpact`. This setting controls execution after the trigger condition is met; it does not change the trigger price itself. Add a limit price instead when the order must never execute beyond a specific absolute price. The trade-off is that the resulting limit order can remain unfilled.

## End-to-end example: stop-loss

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Prerequisites.** EVM examples use [`viem`](https://viem.sh); Solana examples use `@solana/web3.js`, `tweetnacl`, and `bs58`. All requests go to `https://flash.definitive.fi/v1` with your key in the `x-definitive-api-key` header. The public integrator key `dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b` is safe for development. The onchain steps also need an RPC endpoint and the funder wallet's key, supplied here through environment variables.

> [accordion] EVM
>
> Sell 0.05 WETH for USDC on Base if WETH falls to \$3,000 or below. On a sell, `qty` is denominated in the target asset (WETH). If the spent token needs an allowance, the quote returns `evm.approveTx` (or `evm.permitTypedData` on the Permit2 path); handle whichever it returns, then sign the order payload and submit.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { createWalletClient, createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
> import { base } from "viem/chains";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`);
> const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain: base, transport: http(process.env.EVM_RPC_URL) });
> const publicClient = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http(process.env.EVM_RPC_URL) });
>
> const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
>   fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
>     method: "POST",
>     headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>     body: JSON.stringify(body),
>   }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> const order = {
>   targetChain: "base",
>   contraChain: "base",
>   targetAsset: "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
>   contraAsset: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
>   side: "sell",
>   qty: "0.05",
>   orderType: "stop-loss",
>   triggers: [{ notionalPrice: "3000", triggerType: "lower" }],
>   maxPriceImpact: "0.1", // reject execution above 10% price impact
> };
>
> const quote = await post("/quote", { ...order, funderAddress: account.address });
>
> if (quote.evm.approveTx) {
>   const hash = await wallet.sendTransaction({
>     to: quote.evm.approveTx.to,
>     data: quote.evm.approveTx.data,
>     value: 0n,
>   });
>   await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });
> }
>
> let permitFields = {};
> if (quote.evm.permitTypedData) {
>   const evmPermitSignature = await account.signTypedData(JSON.parse(quote.evm.permitTypedData));
>   permitFields = { evmPermitTypedData: quote.evm.permitTypedData, evmPermitSignature };
> }
>
> const { domain, types, primaryType, message } = JSON.parse(quote.evm.orderTypedData);
> const userSignature = await account.signTypedData({ domain, types, primaryType, message });
>
> const { orderId } = await post("/order", {
>   ...order,
>   funderAddress: account.address,
>   quoteId: quote.quoteId,
>   userSignature,
>   evmOrderTypedData: quote.evm.orderTypedData,
>   ...permitFields,
> });
>
> console.log("orderId", orderId);
> ```

> [accordion] SVM (Solana)
>
> Sell 5 WSOL for USDC if WSOL falls to \$120 or below. On a sell, `qty` is denominated in the target asset (WSOL). Before the first trade of a token the swap needs the funder's token accounts (`svm.ataSetupIxs`) and a delegation (`svm.delegateIx` or a sponsor-paid `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx`). Run the onchain steps in order, then sign the order message offchain and submit.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import {
>   Connection,
>   Keypair,
>   PublicKey,
>   TransactionInstruction,
>   TransactionMessage,
>   VersionedTransaction,
> } from "@solana/web3.js";
> import nacl from "tweetnacl";
> import bs58 from "bs58";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");
> const funder = Keypair.fromSecretKey(bs58.decode(process.env.SOLANA_SECRET_KEY!));
>
> const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
>   fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
>     method: "POST",
>     headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>     body: JSON.stringify(body),
>   }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> const toIx = (ix: any) =>
>   new TransactionInstruction({
>     programId: new PublicKey(ix.programId),
>     keys: ix.accounts.map((a: any) => ({
>       pubkey: new PublicKey(a.pubkey),
>       isSigner: a.isSigner,
>       isWritable: a.isWritable,
>     })),
>     data: Buffer.from(bs58.decode(ix.data)),
>   });
>
> async function sendIxs(instructions: any[]) {
>   const { blockhash } = await connection.getLatestBlockhash();
>   const message = new TransactionMessage({
>     payerKey: funder.publicKey,
>     recentBlockhash: blockhash,
>     instructions: instructions.map(toIx),
>   }).compileToV0Message();
>   const tx = new VersionedTransaction(message);
>   tx.sign([funder]);
>   const sig = await connection.sendRawTransaction(tx.serialize());
>   await connection.confirmTransaction(sig, "confirmed");
> }
>
> const order = {
>   targetChain: "solana",
>   contraChain: "solana",
>   targetAsset: "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112", // WSOL
>   contraAsset: "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v", // USDC
>   side: "sell",
>   qty: "5",
>   orderType: "stop-loss",
>   triggers: [{ notionalPrice: "120", triggerType: "lower" }],
>   maxPriceImpact: "0.1", // reject execution above 10% price impact
> };
>
> const quote = await post("/quote", { ...order, funderAddress: funder.publicKey.toBase58() });
>
> if (quote.svm.ataSetupIxs) await sendIxs(quote.svm.ataSetupIxs);
>
> let delegateFields = {};
> if (quote.svm.sponsoredDelegateTx) {
>   const tx = VersionedTransaction.deserialize(Buffer.from(quote.svm.sponsoredDelegateTx, "base64"));
>   tx.sign([funder]);
>   delegateFields = { svmSponsoredDelegateTx: Buffer.from(tx.serialize()).toString("base64") };
> } else if (quote.svm.delegateIx) {
>   await sendIxs([quote.svm.delegateIx]);
> }
>
> const signature = nacl.sign.detached(new TextEncoder().encode(quote.svm.orderMessage), funder.secretKey);
> const userSignature = bs58.encode(signature);
>
> const { orderId } = await post("/order", {
>   ...order,
>   funderAddress: funder.publicKey.toBase58(),
>   quoteId: quote.quoteId,
>   userSignature,
>   svmNonce: quote.svm.nonce,
>   svmDeadline: quote.svm.deadline,
>   ...delegateFields,
> });
>
> console.log("orderId", orderId);
> ```

## Take-profit and stop

The flow above works unchanged for the other two trigger types. Swap the `order` block for one of these; everything else (approval or delegation, signing, submit) stays the same.

**Take-profit: sell 0.05 WETH when it rises to \$5,000 or above.**

```jsonc theme={null}
{
  "targetChain": "base",
  "contraChain": "base",
  "targetAsset": "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
  "contraAsset": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
  "side": "sell",
  "qty": "0.05",
  "orderType": "take-profit",
  "triggers": [{ "notionalPrice": "5000", "triggerType": "upper" }]
}
```

**Stop (breakout buy): spend 100 USDC to buy WETH when it rises to \$5,000 or above.**

On a buy, `qty` is denominated in the contra asset (USDC).

```jsonc theme={null}
{
  "targetChain": "base",
  "contraChain": "base",
  "targetAsset": "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
  "contraAsset": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
  "side": "buy",
  "qty": "100",
  "orderType": "stop",
  "triggers": [{ "notionalPrice": "5000", "triggerType": "upper" }]
}
```

Add a limit price — `limitNotionalPrice` or `limitCrossPrice`, but not both — to any of these for a limit variant (the order becomes a limit order once triggered), and `expireTime` (an ISO-8601 timestamp) for good-til-time behavior. Omit `expireTime` for good-til-cancelled. The limit price and the trigger price choose their basis independently. A `limitPrice` inside `triggers` is for [bracket](/docs/brackets#standalone-brackets) legs only and is rejected on these types.

Once a trigger order is live, you can move its prices without cancelling — see [Updating Orders](/docs/updating-orders). Every type on this page accepts a trigger-price update ("move my stop"), and the `-limit` variants also accept a new post-trigger execution limit — either or both in one update.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To track the order after submit, poll `GET /orders` or stream live updates over the [Orders WebSocket](/docs/api-reference/flash/websocket-orders).

> [card] [Market Order](/docs/market-order)
>
> Execute immediately at the best price.

> [card] [Placing Orders](/docs/placing-orders)
>
> The full parameter reference for every order type.


# TWAP Order
Source: https://flash.definitive.fi/docs/twap-order

End-to-end TWAP order on EVM and Solana. Quote, sign, and submit with runnable TypeScript.

A TWAP (time-weighted average price) order slices one large order into tranches executed over a set duration, reducing price impact. Set the total duration with `durationSeconds`; Flash converts it into the onchain deadline with a 60-second execution buffer. Optionally schedule the start with `startTime`, and bound execution with a limit price. For the concepts behind the parameters, see [Placing Orders](/docs/placing-orders).

This page shows the full flow end to end (quote, sign, submit) as a runnable script for each chain. Both examples sell over one hour: WETH for USDC on Base, and WSOL for USDC on Solana. The signing and submit plumbing is identical to a market order; only the request fields differ.

## TWAP parameters

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `orderType` | Yes | `"twap"` |
| `side` | Yes | `"buy"` or `"sell"` |
| `qty` | Yes | Total spend amount, as a string. Contra units on a buy, target units on a sell |
| `durationSeconds` | Yes | Total duration in seconds. Minimum 300 (5 minutes). Quote-time only — not echoed on submit |
| `twapBucketCount` | Optional | Number of tranches, between 2 and 2560. Echo the same value on submit |
| `startTime` | Optional | ISO-8601 scheduled start. `durationSeconds` is measured from this time. Echo the same value on submit |
| `limitNotionalPrice` | Optional (one basis) | USD limit price for the target asset. Tranches execute only at that price or better |
| `limitCrossPrice` | Optional (one basis) | Pair-rate limit price (target / contra). Mutually exclusive with `limitNotionalPrice` |

Omit `startTime` to begin immediately. A limit price is optional on a TWAP — supply at most one of the two bases; see [Pricing basis](/docs/placing-orders#pricing-basis).

TWAP orders do not accept `expireTime` (the duration sets expiry instead) or `triggers`. Progress is surfaced on the order status through `twapBucketCount` and `completedFillCount`.

## End-to-end example

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Prerequisites.** EVM examples use [`viem`](https://viem.sh); Solana examples use `@solana/web3.js`, `tweetnacl`, and `bs58`. All requests go to `https://flash.definitive.fi/v1` with your key in the `x-definitive-api-key` header. The public integrator key `dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b` is safe for development. The onchain steps also need an RPC endpoint and the funder wallet's key, supplied here through environment variables.

> [accordion] EVM
>
> Sell 5 WETH for USDC on Base, spread over one hour. On a sell, `qty` is denominated in the target asset (WETH). If the spent token needs an allowance, the quote returns `evm.approveTx` (or `evm.permitTypedData` on the Permit2 path); handle whichever it returns, then sign the order payload and submit.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { createWalletClient, createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
> import { base } from "viem/chains";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`);
> const wallet = createWalletClient({ account, chain: base, transport: http(process.env.EVM_RPC_URL) });
> const publicClient = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http(process.env.EVM_RPC_URL) });
>
> const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
>   fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
>     method: "POST",
>     headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>     body: JSON.stringify(body),
>   }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> const order = {
>   targetChain: "base",
>   contraChain: "base",
>   targetAsset: "0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006", // WETH
>   contraAsset: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", // USDC
>   side: "sell",
>   qty: "5",
>   orderType: "twap",
> };
>
> // durationSeconds is a quote-time field, so it is not echoed on submit
> const quote = await post("/quote", { ...order, durationSeconds: 3600, funderAddress: account.address });
>
> if (quote.evm.approveTx) {
>   const hash = await wallet.sendTransaction({
>     to: quote.evm.approveTx.to,
>     data: quote.evm.approveTx.data,
>     value: 0n,
>   });
>   await publicClient.waitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });
> }
>
> let permitFields = {};
> if (quote.evm.permitTypedData) {
>   const evmPermitSignature = await account.signTypedData(JSON.parse(quote.evm.permitTypedData));
>   permitFields = { evmPermitTypedData: quote.evm.permitTypedData, evmPermitSignature };
> }
>
> const { domain, types, primaryType, message } = JSON.parse(quote.evm.orderTypedData);
> const userSignature = await account.signTypedData({ domain, types, primaryType, message });
>
> const { orderId } = await post("/order", {
>   ...order,
>   funderAddress: account.address,
>   quoteId: quote.quoteId,
>   userSignature,
>   evmOrderTypedData: quote.evm.orderTypedData,
>   ...permitFields,
> });
>
> console.log("orderId", orderId);
> ```

> [accordion] SVM (Solana)
>
> Sell 5 WSOL for USDC, spread over one hour. On a sell, `qty` is denominated in the target asset (WSOL). Before the first trade of a token the swap needs the funder's token accounts (`svm.ataSetupIxs`) and a delegation (`svm.delegateIx` or a sponsor-paid `svm.sponsoredDelegateTx`). Run the onchain steps in order, then sign the order message offchain and submit.
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import {
>   Connection,
>   Keypair,
>   PublicKey,
>   TransactionInstruction,
>   TransactionMessage,
>   VersionedTransaction,
> } from "@solana/web3.js";
> import nacl from "tweetnacl";
> import bs58 from "bs58";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const connection = new Connection(process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL!, "confirmed");
> const funder = Keypair.fromSecretKey(bs58.decode(process.env.SOLANA_SECRET_KEY!));
>
> const post = (path: string, body: unknown) =>
>   fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
>     method: "POST",
>     headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>     body: JSON.stringify(body),
>   }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> const toIx = (ix: any) =>
>   new TransactionInstruction({
>     programId: new PublicKey(ix.programId),
>     keys: ix.accounts.map((a: any) => ({
>       pubkey: new PublicKey(a.pubkey),
>       isSigner: a.isSigner,
>       isWritable: a.isWritable,
>     })),
>     data: Buffer.from(bs58.decode(ix.data)),
>   });
>
> async function sendIxs(instructions: any[]) {
>   const { blockhash } = await connection.getLatestBlockhash();
>   const message = new TransactionMessage({
>     payerKey: funder.publicKey,
>     recentBlockhash: blockhash,
>     instructions: instructions.map(toIx),
>   }).compileToV0Message();
>   const tx = new VersionedTransaction(message);
>   tx.sign([funder]);
>   const sig = await connection.sendRawTransaction(tx.serialize());
>   await connection.confirmTransaction(sig, "confirmed");
> }
>
> const order = {
>   targetChain: "solana",
>   contraChain: "solana",
>   targetAsset: "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112", // WSOL
>   contraAsset: "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v", // USDC
>   side: "sell",
>   qty: "5",
>   orderType: "twap",
> };
>
> // durationSeconds is a quote-time field, so it is not echoed on submit
> const quote = await post("/quote", { ...order, durationSeconds: 3600, funderAddress: funder.publicKey.toBase58() });
>
> if (quote.svm.ataSetupIxs) await sendIxs(quote.svm.ataSetupIxs);
>
> let delegateFields = {};
> if (quote.svm.sponsoredDelegateTx) {
>   const tx = VersionedTransaction.deserialize(Buffer.from(quote.svm.sponsoredDelegateTx, "base64"));
>   tx.sign([funder]);
>   delegateFields = { svmSponsoredDelegateTx: Buffer.from(tx.serialize()).toString("base64") };
> } else if (quote.svm.delegateIx) {
>   await sendIxs([quote.svm.delegateIx]);
> }
>
> const signature = nacl.sign.detached(new TextEncoder().encode(quote.svm.orderMessage), funder.secretKey);
> const userSignature = bs58.encode(signature);
>
> const { orderId } = await post("/order", {
>   ...order,
>   funderAddress: funder.publicKey.toBase58(),
>   quoteId: quote.quoteId,
>   userSignature,
>   svmNonce: quote.svm.nonce,
>   svmDeadline: quote.svm.deadline,
>   ...delegateFields,
> });
>
> console.log("orderId", orderId);
> ```

To buy instead, set `side` to `"buy"` and denominate `qty` in the contra asset (for example `"1000"` USDC). Add `twapBucketCount` to control how many tranches the order is split into. To schedule the TWAP and cap its execution price, add `startTime` and a limit price to both the quote and the submit — for example `startTime: "2026-05-12T00:00:00Z"` with `limitNotionalPrice: "4000"` sells only at \$4,000 per WETH or better, starting at that time. `startTime` and `twapBucketCount` must match the values used at quote time; `durationSeconds` is quote-time only.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To track fill progress after submit, poll `GET /orders` or stream live updates over the [Orders WebSocket](/docs/api-reference/flash/websocket-orders). TWAP orders report `completedFillCount` against `twapBucketCount`.

> [card] [Trigger Orders](/docs/trigger-orders)
>
> Stop, stop-loss, and take-profit orders.

> [card] [Market Order](/docs/market-order)
>
> Execute immediately at the best price.

> [card] [Bracket Orders](/docs/brackets)
>
> Attach a take-profit / stop-loss pair to this order at placement.


# Updating Orders
Source: https://flash.definitive.fi/docs/updating-orders

How to change the limit price, trigger price, or bracket legs of a resting Flash order by signing an update message with the funder wallet.

Change the limit price or trigger price of a resting order — move a stop-loss, take profit sooner, reprice a resting limit, move both legs of a bracket — with [`PATCH /orders/{orderId}`](/docs/api-reference/flash/update), no need to cancel and re-place, and the order keeps its `orderId`. Like cancelling, updating requires a **wallet signature** in addition to your API key: you construct a short plaintext message, sign it with the funder wallet, and send both with the new price(s). The update signature is offchain and gasless; no transaction is sent, and the original order signature and token approval stay untouched.

## What can be updated

An update carries a new **limit price**, a new **trigger price**, or both — or, on a bracket, both **legs** — depending on the order type:

| Order type | Limit price | Trigger price | Bracket legs |
| - | - | - | - |
| `limit` | yes | — | — |
| `stop`, `stop-loss`, `take-profit` (no limit price — executes at market once triggered) | — | yes | — |
| `stop-limit` / `take-profit-limit` (placed with a limit price) | yes | yes — either or both in one update | — |
| `bracket` (standalone, or the pair minted by an attached bracket) | — | — | yes — both legs, each with its trigger price and an optional leg limit |
| `trailing-stop`, `trailing-stop-limit` | — | — | — |

`trailing-stop` and `trailing-stop-limit` are not updatable: a `PATCH` returns `422`. Cancel and place a new order to change `trailPercent` or `activationPrice`; see [Trailing Stop Orders](/docs/trailing-stop#lifecycle).

**Limit price** — send exactly one of `limitNotionalPrice` (USD price of the target asset) or `limitCrossPrice` (pair rate, target / contra). You are not restricted to the basis the order was placed with; the order carries whichever basis was set last. On the trigger types the limit is the **post-trigger execution limit**: the price the order fills at once the trigger has fired. See [Pricing basis](/docs/placing-orders#pricing-basis).

**Trigger price** — send a `trigger` object with the same shape as submit's: exactly one of `notionalPrice` or `crossPrice`, plus `triggerType` (`lower` or `upper`). A trigger update moves the **threshold only**:

> [!WARNING]
>
> The trigger's direction and price basis are fixed for the life of the order. `triggerType` must match the direction the trigger was **placed with** — always `lower` for `stop-loss`, always `upper` for `take-profit`, and whichever direction your `stop` order used (typically `upper` for a breakout buy). The price must likewise be in the same basis the trigger was placed with — a trigger placed with `notionalPrice` can only be updated with `notionalPrice`. This differs from the limit price, whose basis you may switch freely. A new trigger price that the market already satisfies is rejected — an update never causes an immediate fire.

**Bracket legs** — send `triggers` with both legs, one `lower` (the stop-loss) and one `upper` (the take-profit), in any order. Each leg carries its new trigger price in the basis it was placed with and an optional `limitPrice`, in the same units as that leg's trigger price (USD for `notionalPrice`, pair rate for `crossPrice`). The update replaces **both legs' prices and limits**: a leg's submitted state is its new state, so a leg sent without `limitPrice` sells at market when it fires, which removes any limit it had. Leg count and directions are fixed, and the same immediate-fire rule applies to each leg. A bracket takes no `trigger` object and no limit fields.

An [attached bracket](/docs/brackets#attached-brackets) is updated through the pair's own order: once the entry has filled, the entry's `attachedBracket.bracketOrderId` is the `orderId` to `PATCH`. Before the first fill `bracketOrderId` is `null` because the pair is not an order yet, so there is nothing to update; `triggers` sent to the entry itself returns `422` on a `market` or `twap` entry and `400` on a `limit` entry. To change the legs before the first fill, cancel the entry and place a new one. An update applies the units above to both legs: for a pair placed before October 27 whose `notionalPrice` leg applied its `limitPrice` as a pair rate, send the new `limitPrice` in USD, and the leg reads it back as a USD price from then on.

To change any other parameter of an order, [cancel](/docs/cancelling-orders) it and place a new one.

## The update message

Construct this exact UTF-8 string — a three-line header followed by one price line per updated value, joined by single newlines:

```text theme={null}
Definitive Flash — Update Order
Order: <orderId>
Issued At: <RFC3339 UTC timestamp>
Limit Notional Price: <newLimitPrice>
Trigger Lower Notional Price: <newTriggerPrice>
```

In code — a stop-limit update moving both prices:

```ts theme={null}
const updateMessage = [
  "Definitive Flash — Update Order",
  `Order: ${orderId}`,
  `Issued At: ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
  `Limit Notional Price: ${newLimitPrice}`,
  `Trigger Lower Notional Price: ${newTriggerPrice}`,
].join("\n");
```

The message bytes are identical on EVM and Solana; only the signing primitive differs. The server validates the message byte-for-byte, so:

* The separator in the header is an **em dash** (`—`, U+2014), not a hyphen. Unlike the cancel header, there is no `v1` — don't copy the header from your cancel flow.

* Line breaks are single `\n` characters. CRLF, blank lines, and a trailing newline are all rejected.

* `<orderId>` is the order's UUID exactly as returned by [`POST /order`](/docs/api-reference/flash/order).

* `Issued At` is an RFC3339 UTC timestamp and must be **within 1 minute** of server time — construct and sign the message immediately before sending. The stamp is what stops a captured signature from being replayed later to revert a newer price. Sub-second precision (e.g. `new Date().toISOString()`) is supported and recommended: two updates on the same order in the same second need distinct stamps to produce distinct signed bytes.

* The **Limit line** is exactly one of `Limit Cross Price: <decimal>` or `Limit Notional Price: <decimal>`, matching the limit field you send in the request body.

* The **Trigger line** is `Trigger <Lower|Upper> <Cross|Notional> Price: <decimal>` — direction matching the `trigger.triggerType` you send (`lower` → `Lower`, `upper` → `Upper`), kind matching which trigger price field is set.

* On a single-trigger order, include only the lines for values you are updating, each at most once, with at least one present; when both are present the **Limit line comes first**.

* A **bracket update** has no Limit line and one Trigger line per leg, the `lower` leg first, each followed by `Trigger <Lower|Upper> Limit Price: <decimal>` only when that leg carries `limitPrice`:

  ```text theme={null}
  Definitive Flash — Update Order
  Order: <orderId>
  Issued At: <RFC3339 UTC timestamp>
  Trigger Lower Notional Price: <newStopLossPrice>
  Trigger Lower Limit Price: <newStopLossLimit>
  Trigger Upper Notional Price: <newTakeProfitPrice>
  ```

* Every decimal must be **byte-identical** to the request value — if the body says `"4000"`, the message must say `4000`, not `4000.0`. No normalization is applied.

Send the exact string you signed back as `updateMessage` in the request body. The message is plaintext by design: a wallet's message-signing prompt shows the user precisely which order is being repriced, and to what.

## Signing the message

Sign with the **funder wallet** — the same wallet that signed the order. A signature from any other key is rejected.

| Chain | Scheme | `userSignature` format |
| - | - | - |
| EVM | EIP-191 `personal_sign` over the message bytes | 65 bytes, `0x`-prefixed hex |
| Solana | Ed25519 over the message bytes | 64 bytes, base58 |

> [!NOTE]
>
> On EVM, the signature is verified onchain against the funder address using ERC-1271 with ERC-6492 support. EOAs, deployed smart accounts, and counterfactual (not-yet-deployed) smart accounts all work — sign with whatever `personal_sign` flow the wallet provides.

## Examples

### Move a stop-loss

The headline use case: raise a resting stop-loss's trigger to \$1,800 (notional basis) without touching anything else. Shown for EVM; on Solana only the signing primitive differs, exactly as in the limit examples below.

```ts theme={null}
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";

const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`);

const orderId = "..."; // from POST /order
const newTriggerPrice = "1800";
const updateMessage = [
  "Definitive Flash — Update Order",
  `Order: ${orderId}`,
  `Issued At: ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
  `Trigger Lower Notional Price: ${newTriggerPrice}`,
].join("\n");
const userSignature = await account.signMessage({ message: updateMessage }); // EIP-191 personal_sign

const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/orders/${orderId}`, {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    trigger: { notionalPrice: newTriggerPrice, triggerType: "lower" },
    updateMessage,
    userSignature,
  }),
}).then((r) => r.json());

console.log(res); // { ok: true }
```

A `take-profit` update is identical with `triggerType: "upper"` and a `Trigger Upper ...` line. On a `stop-limit` or `take-profit-limit` you can move the limit in the same request: add the limit field to the body and its `Limit ... Price:` line to the message, above the trigger line.

### Move both legs of a bracket

Tighten a resting bracket: raise the stop-loss to \$1,800 and have it sell no lower than \$1,774, and lift the take-profit to \$2,400 at market. Both legs are always sent, in any order; the message signs the `lower` leg first with its limit line right after its trigger line. For an attached pair, `orderId` is the entry's `attachedBracket.bracketOrderId`.

```ts theme={null}
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";

const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`);

const orderId = "..."; // the bracket's orderId, or the pair's bracketOrderId
const triggers = [
  { notionalPrice: "1800", triggerType: "lower", limitPrice: "1774" },
  { notionalPrice: "2400", triggerType: "upper" },
];
const updateMessage = [
  "Definitive Flash — Update Order",
  `Order: ${orderId}`,
  `Issued At: ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
  "Trigger Lower Notional Price: 1800",
  "Trigger Lower Limit Price: 1774",
  "Trigger Upper Notional Price: 2400",
].join("\n");
const userSignature = await account.signMessage({ message: updateMessage }); // EIP-191 personal_sign

const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/orders/${orderId}`, {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
  body: JSON.stringify({ triggers, updateMessage, userSignature }),
}).then((r) => r.json());

console.log(res); // { ok: true }
```

To drop a leg's limit, send that leg without `limitPrice` and without its `Limit Price` line; the leg then sells at market when it fires. The order reads the new legs back under `brackets`, on REST and on the WebSocket, once the update applies. For an attached pair, the entry's `attachedBracket` legs on `GET /orders/{orderId}` show the pair's new legs too.

A bracket body with the wrong shape is rejected with `400` before the signature is checked: one or three legs, two legs in the same direction, a leg with both or neither trigger price, a `limitPrice` that is not positive, or `triggers` sent together with `trigger`, `limitNotionalPrice`, or `limitCrossPrice`. Sending a bracket the single-trigger `trigger` object, or a limit field on its own, is `400` as well.

### Reprice a resting limit

Both examples move a resting limit order's price to \$4,000 (notional basis). To price in the pair rate instead, use `Limit Cross Price:` in the message and `limitCrossPrice` in the body.

> [accordion] EVM
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const account = privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY as `0x${string}`);
>
> const orderId = "..."; // from POST /order
> const newPrice = "4000";
> const updateMessage = [
>   "Definitive Flash — Update Order",
>   `Order: ${orderId}`,
>   `Issued At: ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
>   `Limit Notional Price: ${newPrice}`,
> ].join("\n");
> const userSignature = await account.signMessage({ message: updateMessage }); // EIP-191 personal_sign
>
> const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/orders/${orderId}`, {
>   method: "PATCH",
>   headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>   body: JSON.stringify({ limitNotionalPrice: newPrice, updateMessage, userSignature }),
> }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> console.log(res); // { ok: true }
> ```

> [accordion] SVM (Solana)
>
> ```ts theme={null}
> import { Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
> import nacl from "tweetnacl";
> import bs58 from "bs58";
>
> const BASE_URL = "https://flash.definitive.fi/v1";
> const API_KEY = "dpka_513a2bd7_57a2_46d2_927b_2a3857fe271b";
>
> const funder = Keypair.fromSecretKey(bs58.decode(process.env.SOLANA_SECRET_KEY!));
>
> const orderId = "..."; // from POST /order
> const newPrice = "4000";
> const updateMessage = [
>   "Definitive Flash — Update Order",
>   `Order: ${orderId}`,
>   `Issued At: ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
>   `Limit Notional Price: ${newPrice}`,
> ].join("\n");
> const signature = nacl.sign.detached(new TextEncoder().encode(updateMessage), funder.secretKey);
> const userSignature = bs58.encode(signature); // 64-byte Ed25519 signature
>
> const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/orders/${orderId}`, {
>   method: "PATCH",
>   headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-definitive-api-key": API_KEY },
>   body: JSON.stringify({ limitNotionalPrice: newPrice, updateMessage, userSignature }),
> }).then((r) => r.json());
>
> console.log(res); // { ok: true }
> ```

## What an update does

An accepted update is executed as a **cancel-and-replace under the same `orderId`**: the remaining quantity is re-placed with the new price(s), and the order's identity is stable everywhere — [`GET /orders/{orderId}`](/docs/api-reference/flash/get-order), the [Orders WebSocket](/docs/api-reference/flash/websocket-orders), and any state you key by `orderId`.

**Partial fills are kept.** Fills that already settled onchain are final; only the unfilled remainder is re-placed.

**The update is visible on the WebSocket.** While the update is in flight, order frames carry `pendingUpdate: true`; once applied, the flag clears and the frames carry the new `limitNotionalPrice` / `limitCrossPrice` and `trigger`, or the new `brackets` legs. If the flag clears and the prices are unchanged, the update was rejected downstream.

## Which orders can be updated

An order is updatable while it is live and unfilled under its `orderId` — status `ORDER_STATUS_ACCEPTED` or `ORDER_STATUS_PARTIALLY_FILLED`, whether it is resting at a limit or armed waiting on a trigger. See [Order statuses](/docs/order-statuses).

For the trigger types, what is updatable depends on whether the trigger has fired:

* **Before the trigger fires**, the trigger price can move, and on `stop-limit` / `take-profit-limit` the post-trigger execution limit can move with it — either or both in one update.
* **After the trigger fires**, a `stop-limit` / `take-profit-limit` order is an ordinary resting limit order; a limit update reprices it in flight — cancelled and re-placed at the new price under the same `orderId`. A trigger update at that point is rejected: there is no trigger left to move. (`stop` and `take-profit` execute at market on firing, so there is nothing to update after the fire.)

A `bracket` is updatable while neither leg has fired. Once a leg fires the bracket is executing its exit and an update returns `422`; a leg that fires while an update is in flight wins, and the update is rejected downstream: the `PATCH` has already returned `200`, and the order's frames show `pendingUpdate` clearing with the legs unchanged. An attached pair's size grows with its entry's fills, and an update re-checks the same minimum order size placement enforces, against the pair's current size at the new prices — a pair still below the minimum is rejected with `400` (`order below minimum notional size requirement`) until further entry fills have grown it past the minimum; retry after the next fill.

The mechanics below apply to every updatable type:

* **One update at a time.** While an update is in flight, another `PATCH` returns `422` (`order already has a pending update`). Wait for the WebSocket frame with the new price, or re-read the order, before sending the next one.
* **Closed orders can't be updated.** Orders in `ORDER_STATUS_FILLED`, `ORDER_STATUS_CANCELLED` (expired orders included), `ORDER_STATUS_REJECTED`, or `ORDER_STATUS_TERMINATED` return `422` (`order is closed and can no longer be updated`).
* **A `stop`, `stop-loss`, or `take-profit` that fires on entry has nothing to reprice.** If the market already satisfies the trigger the instant the order is placed, it executes without ever resting; a trigger update for it returns `422`, as for any trigger that has fired, and so does any update once it has closed. A `bracket` with a leg already met at placement is closed `REASON_ORDER_TRIGGERED_ON_ENTRY`, so an update for it returns `422` as a closed order.
* **An update can race a fill.** If the order fills before the update lands, the request returns `422` — treat that as the order having executed at the old price, not as a failure to retry.
* **`404` covers a missing order, an order outside your API key's portfolio, and a failed signature.** If you get a `404` for an order you know exists, check the signature and the message bytes.
* **`400` means the request itself can't apply to this order**: a field its type does not take (`trigger` on a `limit` or `bracket`, a limit on a `stop` or `take-profit` or a `bracket`), a trigger in a different direction or basis, a price or leg limit that is not positive, or new prices that would put the order below the minimum order size (`order below minimum notional size requirement`). Fix the request rather than retrying it. An order type that takes no update at all (`market`, `twap`) returns `422`.
